points: Before the first serve, the home captain says if the match is untimed, soft-timed or hard-stop, and what signals the end (a clock or a buzzer).
The timed procedure starts 20 minutes before the end of court time.
Finish the game in progress with no-ad scoring. If a side already has the ad, play one more point. If that makes it deuce, play one deciding point.
Then look at the set score. Two-game lead: that side wins the set. Tied: play a set tiebreak (to 7, win by 2).
One-game difference: play one more no-ad game. A two-game lead ends the set. A tie means a set tiebreak.
If that was the first set, a set tiebreak decides the second set.
If one side has 2 sets, the match is over. If each side has a set, play a 10-point match tiebreak.
Soft-timed: a tiebreak in progress is played to the end.
Hard-stop during a tiebreak: a side ahead by 2 points wins it. Tied or ahead by 1, it is recorded as a tie.
If a court ends tied, the visiting team is marked as the winner in TennisLink, because the system needs a winner.
Play stays continuous: 25 seconds between points, 90 seconds at changeovers.
Captains may come onto the court to help with the timed procedure only if the players on court ask them.

questions.q: When does the timed procedure start?
options: 10 minutes before the end of court time
15 minutes before the end of court time
20 minutes before the end of court time
30 minutes before the end of court time
questions.why: The timed procedure begins 20 minutes before the end of court time.

questions.q: Who tells the players if the match is untimed, soft-timed or hard-stop, and what signals the end?
options: The home captain, before the first serve
The visiting captain, before the first serve
The players on court, at the 20-minute mark
The club front desk, when time is up
questions.why: The home captain must tell their team and the visiting captain how the match is timed, and what signals the end: a specific clock or a buzzer.

questions.q: The 20-minute mark comes while you are at 30-15 in a game. What do you do with this game?
options: Finish it with no-ad scoring
Stop it and go straight to a tiebreak
Finish it with normal scoring
Start the game again with no-ad scoring
questions.why: At the 20-minute mark, finish the game in progress using no-ad scoring.

questions.q: The timed procedure has started and the game in progress reaches deuce. What happens?
options: One deciding point
Play on until a side wins by two points
The server wins the game
The game is dropped and a tiebreak starts
questions.why: The game in progress is finished with no-ad scoring. At deuce, one point decides the game.

questions.q: The 20-minute mark comes when one side already has the ad. What do you do?
options: Play one more point. If it goes back to deuce, play one deciding point
The side with the ad wins the game
Go back to deuce and play one deciding point
Play on with normal scoring until the game ends
questions.why: If a side already has the ad when the procedure starts, play one more point. If that makes it deuce, play a deciding point.

questions.q: You finish the game in progress. The set score is now 5-3. What happens?
options: The side with 5 wins the set
Play one more no-ad game
Play a set tiebreak
Play on until someone reaches 6
questions.why: With a two-game lead, that side wins the set.

questions.q: You finish the game in progress. The set score is now 4-3. What happens?
options: Play one more no-ad game
The side with 4 wins the set
Play a set tiebreak right away
Play two more no-ad games
questions.why: With a one-game difference, play one more no-ad game.

questions.q: At 4-3 you play the one extra no-ad game. The side that was ahead wins it, so it is 5-3. What happens?
options: The set is over, 5-3
Play one more no-ad game
Play a set tiebreak
Play on until someone reaches 6
questions.why: If the extra game gives a two-game lead, the set is over.

questions.q: At 4-3 you play the one extra no-ad game. The side that was behind wins it, so it is 4-4. What happens?
options: Play a set tiebreak: to 7, win by 2
Play one more no-ad game
Play a 10-point match tiebreak
The set is recorded as a tie
questions.why: If the extra game makes it a tie, play a set tiebreak (to 7, win by 2).

questions.q: You finish the game in progress. The set score is now 3-3. What happens?
options: Play a set tiebreak: to 7, win by 2
Play one more no-ad game
Play two more no-ad games
The set is recorded as a tie
questions.why: If the set is tied after the game in progress, play a set tiebreak (to 7, win by 2).

questions.q: The set you just ended under the timed procedure was the first set. How is the second set decided?
options: By a set tiebreak
By a 10-point match tiebreak
It is not played. The first set decides the match
By one no-ad game
questions.why: If the set that ended was the first set, play a set tiebreak to decide the second set.

questions.q: After the timed procedure each side has won one set. What happens?
options: Play a 10-point match tiebreak
Play a 7-point tiebreak
The match is recorded as a tie
The winner of the first set wins the match
questions.why: If each side has a set, play a 10-point match tiebreak.

questions.q: After the timed procedure one side has won both sets. What happens?
options: The match is over
Play a match tiebreak anyway
Play on until the court time ends
Play one more no-ad game
questions.why: If one side has 2 sets, the match is over.

questions.q: Soft-timed match. Court time runs out in the middle of a tiebreak. What happens?
options: Play the tiebreak to the end
Stop. Whoever is ahead wins
Stop. It is recorded as a tie
Play one deciding point
questions.why: In a soft-timed match, any tiebreak in progress is played to the end.

questions.q: Hard-stop match. The buzzer goes during the match tiebreak at 7-5. What is the result?
options: The side with 7 wins the match
The match is recorded as a tie
Play one more point
Play on until someone reaches 10
questions.why: At a hard stop during a match tiebreak, whoever is ahead by 2 points wins the match.

questions.q: Hard-stop match. The buzzer goes during the match tiebreak at 6-5. What is the result?
options: The match is recorded as a tie
The side with 6 wins the match
Play one more point
Play on until someone leads by 2
questions.why: At a hard stop, a side that is tied or ahead by only 1 point does not win. The match is recorded as a tie.

questions.q: Hard-stop match. The buzzer goes during a set tiebreak at 5-3. What is the result of the set?
options: The side with 5 wins the set
The set is recorded as a tie
Play on until someone reaches 7
Play one deciding point
questions.why: At a hard stop during a set tiebreak, whoever is ahead by 2 points wins the set. Tied or ahead by 1, the set is recorded as a tie.

questions.q: Your court ends in a tie. Who is marked as the winner in TennisLink?
options: The visiting team
The home team
Nobody. A tie is entered
The team that won the first set
questions.why: If a court ends tied, the visiting team is marked as the winner in TennisLink, because the system requires a winner.

questions.q: In the last 20 minutes, how much time do you have between points and at changeovers?
options: The same as always: 25 seconds and 90 seconds
Half the usual time
No breaks at all, not even for water
As long as both sides agree
questions.why: Play stays continuous: 25 seconds between points and 90 seconds on changeovers. Water and a towel are fine, but the clocks still apply.

questions.q: In the last 20 minutes, when may a captain come onto your court to help with the timed procedure?
options: Only if the players on court ask
Any time the captain sees a mistake
Only if both captains come together
Never
questions.why: Captains may come onto the court to help with timed procedures only if the players on court ask them to.
